title: GW Ori: Interactions between a Triple-star System and Its Circumtriple Disk in Action
question: What substructures (rings, eccentricity, misalignment) does the circumtriple disk of GW Ori have, and do they indicate ongoing interactions with the triple stars?

what.value: Stellar masses ~2.7, 1.7, 0.9 Msun and AB-C orbit inclination/node

evidence.quote: The stellar masses have been constrained to be $\sim$ 2.7, 1.7, and 0.9 $M_\odot$, respectively (cite: czekala2017).
The stellar luminosity modified by the distance provided by GAIA DR2 is 49.3 $\pm$ 7.4 $L_{\odot}$ (cite: calvet2004; gaia2018).

what.value: Dust opacity 10 cm2/g at 1000 GHz, index 1

evidence.quote: We assume a dust grain opacity of 10 cm^2^ g^-1^ at 1000 GHz with a power-law index of 1 (cite: beckwith1990).

recipe.method: Pipeline calibration, phase self-cal, CASA CLEAN with uniform weighting (continuum) and Briggs robust 0.5 (CO)
Optically thin dust mass equation with ring-radius dependent dust temperature
assumptions: T_dust = 30 (L/38 Lsun)^1/4 (r/100 AU)^-1/2; kappa 10 cm2/g at 1000 GHz, index 1; d=402 pc

recipe.method: Three Gaussian-profile rings fitted in visibilities; Model 1 independent inclined circular rings; Models 2/3 eccentric inner ring
DALI models with three annuli of different inclination/PA, run through ALMA simulator, compared with first-moment map against coplanar model by eye
key_parameters: disk mass 0.12 Msun, Sigma_c=3 g/cm2, rc=320 AU, gamma=1.0, (h/r)c=0.18, psi=0.1, gas-to-dust 100

recipe.method: Analytic radial communication, precession and alignment timescales; PHANTOM SPH simulation with 10^6 particles
key_parameters: alpha_AV=0.31, h/r=0.05, disk mass 0.1 Msun, 40-400 AU

evidence.quote: We identify three dust rings with different apparent shapes in the disk at $\sim$ 46, 188, and 338 AU
We estimate the dust masses of the rings to be 74 $\pm$ 8, 168 $\pm$ 19, and 245 $\pm$ 28 $M_\oplus$, respectively
The continuum flux densities of the inner, middle, and outer ring are 42 $\pm$ 4, 95 $\pm$ 10 and 58 $\pm$ 6 mJy, respectively.
The integrated flux density of the disk (195 $\pm$ 20 mJy)

answer_key.quantity: Global precession and radial communication timescales

evidence.quote: the global precession time-scale of the entire disk is $\sim$ 0.83 Myr, and the radial communication time-scale is $\sim$ 0.06 Myr

not_stated_but_needed: CLEAN threshold, mask, cell and image size, number of iterations
Self-calibration reference model and how many rounds
MCMC priors' numeric bounds, initial walker positions, and convergence checks
DALI chemistry and model setup details beyond Table 4
score_reason: Single public dataset and a clear model structure, but imaging parameters and fitting details are incomplete.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, numeric ring radii, masses and ring-fit parameters can be reproduced with moderate assumptions.
